reason: The quote states that with Provisioned IOPS (SSD) storage you specify an IOPS rate when creating a DB instance and RDS provisions that rate for the lifetime of the DB instance.
The quote states a point-in-time restore can specify any second during the retention period up to the Latest Restorable Time, which is typically within the last five minutes.
The quote and its context present public web subnet plus private RDS subnet as 'one way' to use a VPC; the claim's word 'common' is not stated in the quote.
The quote states that by default customers are allowed up to a total of 40 RDS DB instances; the second quote shows more can be requested with the request form (adjustable).
The quote states that of those default 40, up to 10 can be RDS for Oracle or RDS for SQL Server DB instances under the License Included model.
The quote states RDS runs a fully managed relational database while offloading database administration, and a database AMI on EC2 lets you manage your own relational database.
Under the question whether read replicas support synchronous replication, the answer is No and the quote states the five engines use native asynchronous replication.
The quotes state a read replica is billed as a standard DB instance at the same rates and replication data transfer within the same AWS Region is not charged.
The quote states RDS for MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL and Oracle allow Multi-AZ configuration on read replicas for disaster recovery and to minimize downtime from engine upgrades.
Under the cross-Region read replica question, the quote states the time until data is available on the replica depends on the network latency between the two Regions.
The quote states a read replica may be used for disaster recovery of the source DB instance in the same AWS Region or in another Region.

The quote, under the question about a Multi-AZ source, says to associate a read replica with a Multi-AZ deployment; the next context sentence gives write availability, durability and read scalability.
The quote states the number of seconds the read replica is behind the primary is published as the CloudWatch metric Replica Lag.
The quotes state RDS for MySQL can permit DDL on a read replica by setting read_only to 0 in its parameter group, and RDS for PostgreSQL does not currently support DDL on a read replica.
The quote states automatic backups must be enabled on the source (retention other than 0) before adding read replicas and must remain enabled for read replicas to work.
The quote states read replicas of read replicas are not currently supported for RDS for Oracle and RDS for SQL Server.
The quotes state you connect to a read replica like a standard DB instance by retrieving its endpoint, and with multiple replicas the application decides how read traffic is distributed.
The quote lists business reporting as a read replica use case: reporting queries can run against a read replica rather than the primary production DB instance.
The quote states an RDS for MySQL or MariaDB read replica stays active and continues accepting read traffic after its source DB instance is deleted.
The quote states deleting an RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance with read replicas promotes all replicas to standalone DB instances that accept read and write traffic.
The quote states Aurora, RDS for MySQL and MariaDB can create three tiers of read replicas; the context describes second- and third-tier replicas of replicas.
Under 'Common reasons for deploying a read replica', the quote lists scaling beyond the compute or I/O capacity of a single DB instance for read-heavy workloads.
The quote states required software patching is automatically scheduled only for patches that are security and durability related.
The quote states a restore to a point in time or from a DB snapshot creates a new DB instance with a new endpoint.
The quote states automated backups can be turned off by setting the retention period to 0, marked not recommended.
The quote states the retention period is 7 days by default and can be set to up to 35 days.
The quote states the retention value cannot be set to 0 if the DB instance is a source to read replicas.
The quote states you cannot cancel a reserved DB instance and the one-time payment, if applicable, is not refundable.
The quote states that with an engine and license model supporting size flexibility, a Multi-AZ reserved instance covers usage for two Single-AZ DB instances; the condition is kept.
Under the question whether RIs are available for Multi-AZ (answer Yes), the quote states you can select the Multi-AZ option when purchasing a reserved instance.
The quote states RDS RIs are purchased for a Region rather than an Availability Zone and therefore are not capacity reservations.
The quote states there are three RI payment options: No Upfront, Partial Upfront and All Upfront.
The quote states a DB instance reservation can be applied to a read replica provided the DB instance class and Region are the same.
The quote states each RI's Region is fixed for the lifetime of the reservation and cannot be changed, but it can be used in any available AZ in that Region.
The quote states a reservation for size-flexible engines (MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Aurora, Oracle BYOL) applies to any size in the same instance family for the same engine and Region.
The quote states RDS RIs reserve a DB instance for a one or three year term for a significant discount compared to on-demand pricing.
The quote states that beyond the largest instance class or maximum storage allocation you can implement partitioning, spreading data across multiple DB instances.
The quote states DB snapshots are user-initiated, can be taken as frequently as you wish, and are kept until you explicitly delete them.
Under the question on databases per DB instance, the quote line states RDS for SQL Server: up to 100 databases per instance.
The quote states SSL/TLS encryption is a compute-intensive operation and will increase the latency of the database connection.
